analysis.title: GS US TMT ... today ..
key_insights: NDX futures rallied about 400 bps from overnight lows, while the NDX outperformed Semis (SOX) by nearly 460 bps on the day, a top 10 daily spread in 10+ years. Semis continue to move further below their 200-dma, with INTC, CBRS, MRVL, TER, CAT and FFIV described as oversold.

Investor conversations focus on the magnitude of moves more than direction, and on when the market may over-price potential policy outcomes if the moves extend beyond today. Examples cited: CSPs outperforming Semis, drawdowns in IPPs or E&Cs, and a sharp rally in consumer discretionary.

With earnings, AI datapoints and conference season fading, attention turns to policy narratives through the end of 2026. Oil is at 1-month lows and 30yr and 10yr yields are back to mid-September levels. The desk cites GS Econ's election recap, which expects data center moratoria to fade in importance and not be long-lived if enacted.

AMD is flat on the day after being up 9% the prior night. The desk sees no earnings-related reason for the fade. AMD addressed 2027 gross margins (GSe raised its '27 GMs to 55.7%) and 4Q/2027 revenue despite PC headwinds, with data center strength and guidance for >80% revenue growth in '27. The debate likely shifts to the multiple as GPUs mix in and Semis de-rate.

ANET is up 5% after being up 10% the prior night, described as possibly one of the better prints of this AI cycle. Revenue accelerated into the 50s y/y and CY'27 revenue started at +38-40% y/y versus expectations near ~30%. The only pushbacks are the q/q decline in deferred revenue and decelerating bookings growth. GIR is now slightly below ~$8 in non-GAAP EPS for '28.

Semiconductor forward multiples compressed more than 40% over two months, from 28x to 16x. The SOX's ~2x forward P/E discount to the S&P 500 is near the widest in 15 years. The desk expects the debate to center on what got priced in.

BKNG is up 11%, one of its biggest 1-day moves in 10+ years. Drivers cited are positioning (~20mn shares short in Bloomberg), valuation (15+ year low in forward EV/EBITDA into the print), and a perceived 'last cut' dynamic with a +1-3% room night guide for 4Q, helped by the oil and rates move. Consensus remains at +HSD y/y growth in room nights and gross bookings for '27.

Brent is having one of its biggest 5-day declines in recent history, down about $18 over five days, producing a ~15pt spread between Energy and Consumer Discretionary GICS sectors over the last 5 sessions. A chart of US Internet vs the S&P 500 against inverted oil is said to explain some of the day's action.

Top inbound questions: AMZN outperformance, a broad Internet rally (EXPE, DASH, APP), Apple back at all-time highs, FLEX down 14%, earnings move magnitudes in DUOL, YOU and BKNG, and DDOG feedback and read-through to consumption.
MSFT registered a new all-time high, a turnaround from the narrative overhang it faced for much of 2H'25/1H'26.

Over 30 TMT names report tonight: AMC, AMPL, APP, ARM, CGNX, CHYM, COHR, CPAY, CRUS, DDD, EXPE, FICO, FIG, FSLY, GTM, HUBS, KVYO, LUMN, MELI, MGNI, MKSI, MSI, PAYC, POWI, PTC, PTRN, QCOM, RPD, SBGI, SNAP, SEZL, TKO, VECO, VERX, VIAV, WU, WOLF, ZG. Pre-market tomorrow: FWONK, SPHR, Unity.
